AdminDoc-X — AI-Powered Document Understanding System
GitHub: github.com/ayamekni/AdminDoc-X Type: Academic project — ESPRIM Status: Completed Stack: Python, OCR (Tesseract), OpenCV, LayoutLMv3 (fine-tuned), NER, Flask REST API, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, HuggingFace What AdminDoc-X is: AdminDoc-X is an end-to-end document intelligence platform designed to automate the analysis and understanding of administrative documents. It processes unstructured PDFs — invoices, forms, certificates, reports — through a multi-stage AI pipeline, converting them into structured, machine-readable data. The core AI pipeline works as follows: first, OCR using Tesseract with OpenCV preprocessing extracts raw text and bounding boxes from scanned documents. Then layout-aware document understanding is applied. Then a fine-tuned LayoutLMv3 model performs Named Entity Recognition (NER) to extract key fields. Finally post-processing and normalization produce a clean structured JSON output. Extracted fields include entities, dates, identifiers, amounts, and references from complex and heterogeneous document layouts. The system is robust to noisy scans and layout variability. It supports multi-class document type classification. The architecture is modular, enabling extension to new document types. It is scalable for operational and enterprise environments. The backend exposes a production-style Flask REST API (CORS-enabled) returning structured JSON per document. The frontend is built with React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS, showcasing the full pipeline with interactive demo sections.

ATHENA — AI-Powered Educational Platform
GitHub: github.com/ayamekni/athena-ai-education-assistant Medium article: medium.com/@ayamekni2001/athena-from-classical-nlp-to-modern-llms-building-an-intelligent-educational-assistant-1025860c7ca6 Type: Academic/personal project Status: Completed Stack: FastAPI, Python, MongoDB Atlas, LangChain, FAISS, TinyLlama 1.1B, Sentence Transformers, PyTorch (CUDA), JWT, Motor (async MongoDB driver), Docker What ATHENA is: ATHENA is an AI-enhanced educational backend platform that turns raw course content into interactive tutoring, quizzes, and analytics for students, teachers, and admins. It uses RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) with FAISS vector search and a GPU-accelerated TinyLlama 1.1B LLM for context-aware question answering grounded in course materials. It features an intelligent quiz system with 500+ curated questions across Python, Machine Learning, Deep Learning, NLP, and Computer Vision, supporting dynamic quiz generation with 1–50 questions, multiple difficulty levels, and auto-grading with instant feedback. It implements role-based access control (RBAC) with three roles: student, teacher, and admin. Authentication uses JWT (access + refresh tokens) with bcrypt password hashing. It has a room-based conversation system with persistent chat history stored in MongoDB, allowing context-aware multi-turn conversations. The backend is fully async using FastAPI with Motor for async MongoDB operations, Pydantic v2 for input validation, and Swagger/ReDoc for API documentation. Aya also wrote a Medium article about ATHENA covering the journey from classical NLP techniques to modern LLM integration.

ARIA — Agentic Research Intelligence Assistant
GitHub: github.com/ayamekni/ARIA Type: Personal project Status: Completed Stack: LangGraph, LangChain, FastAPI, ChromaDB, PostgreSQL, Plotly, Streamlit, Docker, OpenAI GPT-4o / Mistral, text-embedding-3-small, E2B sandbox, GitHub Actions What ARIA is: ARIA is a multi-agent conversational system that allows any user — technical or not — to ask complex questions about data in natural language and receive executed SQL queries, Python analyses, interactive visualizations, and natural language explanations in return. The architecture uses LangGraph to orchestrate 5 specialized agents: an Analyst Agent that understands intent and decomposes questions; a SQL Agent that generates and executes SQL with automatic error correction and retry; a Python Agent that generates and executes Python code in a secure sandbox; a Visualization Agent that produces interactive Plotly charts; and a Synthesis Agent that explains results in natural language. ARIA implements dual memory: short-term memory via LangGraph State preserving session context with automatic summarization beyond 10 turns, and long-term memory via ChromaDB storing vectorized analyses with semantic search over history. The Python code execution uses a secure sandbox (E2B or isolated subprocess) with whitelisted imports (pandas, numpy, matplotlib, plotly), execution timeout of 30 seconds, and automatic LLM-based error correction with up to 3 retry attempts. The frontend is built with Streamlit featuring a chat interface, searchable analysis history, real-time agent status indicators, and expandable SQL/Python code viewers.

MLOps E2E Pipeline — Lung Cancer Prediction
GitHub: github.com/ayamekni/mlops-lung-cancer-pipeline Medium article: medium.com/@ayamekni2001/from-model-training-to-scalable-deployment-understanding-the-fundamentals-of-mlops-156c0a21ba76 Type: Academic/personal project Status: Completed Stack: Python, Scikit-learn, Gradient Boosting, FastAPI, MLflow, Makefile, Docker, Elasticsearch, Kibana, CI/CD What the MLOps pipeline is: This is a fully automated end-to-end MLOps pipeline for lung cancer prediction from a tabular CSV dataset with demographic and behavioral features. The pipeline covers: environment initialization via Makefile (creating virtual environments and installing dependencies), FastAPI server deployment via Uvicorn, model training triggered via POST /api/train (data loading, preprocessing, class imbalance handling with imbalanced-learn, feature engineering, Gradient Boosting training, MLflow experiment tracking), and model inference via POST /api/predict returning structured JSON predictions. MLflow tracks all parameters, metrics, and versioned model artifacts. The pipeline is fully reproducible — rebuilding from scratch produces consistent results. The modular FastAPI structure supports containerization with Docker. Aya also wrote a Medium article covering MLOps fundamentals and the full implementation.
